title: The Missing Survey: A Team Learns to Check Its Data · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: The Brightline Marketing Team was excited. They had just finished a small survey about a new coffee shop, and the results looked great. Forty people answered the survey. Thirty-two said they would buy coffee there every week. The team leader, Maya, said, "If 80 percent of people say yes, then we should open the shop next month." Everyone agreed. They started to plan the opening. But one team member, Leo, was not sure. He looked at the survey again. "Wait," he said. "We only asked people in our office building. And most of them are coffee drinkers already. If we ask people in other places, the answer might be different." Maya stopped. She looked at the numbers. "You are right," she said. "We have data, but it is not complete data." The team decided to check their conclusion. They made a new plan.
prompt:
Part 1
Do you often look at numbers or data in your daily life?
When you buy something, do you ask your friends for advice?
Do you think small groups of people can give good information?
What do you do when you are not sure about a decision?

Part 2
Describe a time when you or someone you know made a decision with incomplete information. You should say: what the decision was; what information was missing; what happened as a result; and what you learned from it.

Part 3
Why do some people make conclusions too quickly?
How can a team check its data before making a decision?
Do you think surveys are useful for small businesses? Why or why not?
What is more important: a large group of answers or a varied group of answers?
